rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi presents the path of those favored by God as a station of extraordinary rank, whose beginnings become visible through the preceding exposition.
rows.anchor: فما أجل هذه المقامات وأعظم مراتب هذه الدرجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra contains inexhaustible discussions and secrets; the claim that it contains ten thousand questions suits the audience's understanding of its vast implications.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مشتملة على مباحث لا نهاية لها ، وأسرار لا غاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi illustrates how analyzing Aʿūdhu billāh requires definitions and subdivisions of nouns, verbs, particles, and the possible derivations of the name Allah.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن تحصيل به العلم كما ينبغي إلا بعد معرفة الاسم والفعل والحرف أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inquiry can descend from words into speech and phonetics, respiratory and vocal anatomy, sensory qualities, philosophical categories, substances, accidents, existence, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: المباحث المتعلقة بالصوت وكيفية حدوثه وكيفية العضلات المحدثة للأصوات والحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the furthest epistemological stage, he asks how the unknown can be judged contrary to the known if its nature is unknown, since that judgment would make it known.
rows.anchor: فلما حكمنا على غير المعلوم بكونه مقابلا للمعلوم ، وجب أن يكون غير المعلوم معلوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second method counts every proof, objection, reply, and separately stated linguistic alternative as its own question, multiplying the issues extracted from a short passage.
rows.anchor: كل واحد من تلك الوجوه والدلائل مسألة بنفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi distinguishes ordinary derivation from greater derivation, which studies permutations of a word's consonants; he gives 2, 6, 24, and 120 permutations for words of two through five letters.
rows.anchor: أما الاشتقاق الأصغر فمثل اشتقاق صيغة الماضي والمستقبل من المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Greater derivation is difficult beyond triliteral roots because quadriliteral and quinqueliteral permutations proliferate and are mostly unused; even triliteral roots often have unused permutations.
rows.anchor: كأنه لا يمكن رعايته إلا في الكلمات الثلاثية لأن تقاليبها لا تزيد على الستة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says five permutations of ك ل م are attested and share force or intensity: speech affects hearing and mind, a wound, rough ground, striking, kneading, and power.
rows.anchor: تركيب الكاف واللام والميم بحسب تقاليبها الممكنة الستة تفيد القوة والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalima can denote one word or extended connected speech; the latter is metaphorical, by part-for-whole naming or because connected speech resembles a single unit.
rows.anchor: إطلاق لفظ الكلمة على المركب مجاز ، وذلك لوجهين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾānic uses of kalima include Jesus, created by God's command or in a short time, and God's acts, called His words; both uses are explained by the preceding metaphorical grounds.
rows.anchor: يقال لعيسى كلمة الله ، إما لأنه حدث بقوله «كن » أو لأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reads the six permutations of ق و ل as expressing movement or lightness, explaining qawl as easy on the tongue and adducing examples such as the swift bird and animal.
rows.anchor: هذا التركيب بحسب تقاليبه الستة يدل على الحركة والخفة

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī derives lugha from laghawtu, meaning I spoke, and proposes an original form ending in wāw, supported by related forms such as kurra and qulla.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني رحمه الله تعالى : اللغة فعلة من لغوت أي : تلكمت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi supplements Ibn Jinnī with all six permutations of ل غ و and suggests their shared sense is deep engagement or immersion in something.
rows.anchor: ويشبه أن يكون القدر المشترك بين الكل هو الإمعان في الشيء والخوض التام فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He treats lafẓ, literally throwing, as metaphorical for spoken sounds: breath is expelled, and the letters produced by that breath are as if thrown outward.
rows.anchor: وأقول : أظن أن إطلاق اللفظ على هذه الأصوات والحروف على سبيل المجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The permutations of ʿ-b-r share crossing or transition: speech moves between letters and transfers meaning to a hearer, with related examples including tears, crossing, and interpretation.
rows.anchor: وتركيبها من «ع ب ر » وهي في تقاليبها الستة تفيد العبور والانتقال

rows.speaker: النحويون
rows.claim: Most grammarians define kalima as a single word and kalām as a meaningful sentence; Ibn Jinnī sides with them, though Razi finds his evidence weak.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر النحوين : الكلمة غير الكلام ، فالكلمة هي اللفظة المفردة

rows.speaker: الأصوليون
rows.claim: Most legal theorists see no difference between kalima and kalām: either term may cover a single utterance or a compound expression.
rows.anchor: وقال أكثر الأصوليين إنه لا فرق بينهما ، فكل واحد منهما يتناول المفرد والمركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi judges Ibn Jinnī's case for distinguishing kalima from kalām weak, resting chiefly on an implication he draws from a statement by Sībawayh.
rows.anchor: وما رأيت في كلامه حجة قوية في الفرق

rows.speaker: الأصوليون
rows.claim: Legal theorists argue that a single word counts as speech because it opposes silence, affects a listener through meaning, and can naturally be described as something a person said.
rows.anchor: العقلاء قد اتفقوا على أن الكلام ما يضاد الخرس والسكوت

rows.speaker: زفر
rows.claim: In an unconsummated marriage, Zufar says that repeating the conditional phrase إن كلمتك completes the condition before the divorce clause, so the ensuing divorce does not take effect.
rows.anchor: وحجة زفر أنه لما قال في المرة الثانية إن كلمتك

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his two companions treat the condition as incomplete until the whole sentence is finished, so one divorce takes effect when the sentence is complete.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة وصاحباه : تنعقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the disagreement applies to إن كلمتك فأنت طالق; with إن تكلمت بكلمة, إن نطقت, إن تلفظت بلفظة, or إن قلت قولا, Zufar's view should prevail unanimously.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يكون الحق في جميع هذه المسائل قول زفر قولا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars disagree whether kalima and kalām include meaningless speech: some say yes because it can be called unused or unintelligible speech, while others require meaningful expression.
rows.anchor: لفظ الكلمة والكلام هل يتناول المهمل أم لا ؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars also dispute whether naturally meaningful sounds, such as pain cries, coughs, or bird calls, count as words; the issue affects whether hearing one triggers an oath.
rows.anchor: فهل تسمى أمثالها كلمات ؟ وكذلك صوت القطا يشبه كأنه يقول قطا

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī says qawl literally applies to a sentence or a single word, kalām only to a complete sentence, and kalima only to an isolated word; a poem treating qāf as a qawl supports the first distinction.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني : لفظ القول يقع على الكلام التام ، وعلى الكلمة الواحدة

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī says qawl can metaphorically mean a belief or opinion, as in attributing a doctrine to Abū Ḥanīfa or Mālik, because belief is apprehended through its expression.
rows.anchor: لفظ القول يصح جعله مجازا عن الاعتقادات والآراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qāla can be used for nonverbal events, as when birds, eyes, or a full basin are said to speak; Razi also cites two Qurʾānic examples of such speech.
rows.anchor: لفظ قال قد يستعمل في غير النطق

rows.speaker: مثبتو كلام النفس
rows.claim: Those who affirm inner speech say the inward meaning is itself called kalām and qawl; they cite the hypocrites' false claim to be witnesses and Umar's recollection of an inwardly prepared speech.
rows.anchor: فوجب أن يقال إنهم كانوا كاذبين في كلام آخر سوى اللفظ

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A report from ʿUmar says that at the Saqīfa he had composed words within himself, but Abū Bakr spoke first; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: ما نقل أن عمر قال يوم السقيفة : كنت قد زورت في نفسي كلاما

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: The poet al-Akhṭal is cited for the claim that speech resides in the heart and the tongue serves as its guide; Razi gives no grading.
rows.anchor: وأما الشاعر فقول الأخطل : إن الكلام لفي الفؤاد وإنما

rows.speaker: من أنكر كلام النفس
rows.claim: Those denying inner speech argue that someone who neither speaks nor pronounces letters is described as not having spoken, and that oaths attach to uttered words.
rows.anchor: بأن من لم ينطق ولم يتلفظ بالحروف يقال إنه لم يتكلم

rows.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some of Razi's school hold that qawl and kalām are equivocal terms for both the inward meaning and the spoken expression.
rows.anchor: ومن أصحابنا من قال : اسم القول والكلام مشترك بين المعنى النفساني وبين اللفظ اللساني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Utterances are called aḥādīth because their successive letters occur one after another, or because hearing them brings knowledge and meanings into hearts.
rows.anchor: هذه الكلمات والعبارات قد تسمى أحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi lists kalima, kalām, qawl, lafẓ, ʿibāra, ḥadīth, and nuṭq as terms needing comparison, leaving the derivation and precise relation of nuṭq for inquiry.
rows.anchor: وسابعها النطق ويجب البحث عن كيفية اشتقاقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects al-Zamakhsharī's definition of kalima as an utterance denoting one simple meaning by convention: past-tense forms and imperative particles convey more than one element.
rows.anchor: الكلمة هي اللفظة الدالة على معنى مفرد بالوضع ، وهذا التعريف ليس بجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Used expressions divide into a simple form, a compound whose parts signify only in another analysis, and a composed expression whose parts signify independently in every analysis.
rows.anchor: اللفظ المفرد كقولنا فرس وجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meaningful sound has four form-meaning combinations: both simple, both compound, simple form with compound meaning, or compound form with compound meaning; compound form with simple meaning is impossible.
rows.anchor: المسموع المفيد ينقسم إلى أربعة أقسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi defines kalima as a single conventional utterance signifying a meaning; the definition excludes non-words and compounds through its four restrictions.
rows.anchor: الكلمة هي اللفظة المفردة الدالة بالاصطلاح على معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects Avicenna's definition of kalima as a single meaningful sound: sound is a remote genus, whereas lafẓ is the more suitable proximate genus.
rows.anchor: الصوت جنس بعيد ، واللفظ جنس قريب ، وإيراد الجنس القريب أولى

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila require an informative word to contain at least two letters; they explain one-letter particles as shortened forms, but Razi notes that many useful particles remain counterexamples.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : الشرط في كون الكلمة مفيدة أن تكون مركبة من حرفين فصاعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's preferred definition is anything spoken that conveys something by convention; it includes simple and compound forms while excluding writing and gesture.
rows.anchor: كل منطوق به أفاد شيئا بالوضع فهو كلمة

rows.speaker: عباد
rows.claim: ʿAbbād holds that words naturally signify their meanings; Razi rejects this because natural properties do not vary across places and times, and answers that conventional assignments need not be unmotivated.
rows.anchor: دلالة الألفاظ على مدلولاتها ليست ذاتية حقيقية ، خلافا لعباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some words imitate their referents' sounds: qaṭā and laqlaq echo birds, while khaḍm and qaḍm distinguish eating moist and dry foods; Ibn Jinnī gives further examples.
rows.anchor: وضعوا لفظ «الخضم » لأكل الرطب نحو البطيخ والقثاء ، ولفظ «القضم » لأكل اليابس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says one cannot decide whether language was divinely instituted: the regress argument for divine origin and the appeal to God's teaching Adam both admit alternatives.
rows.anchor: لا يمكننا القطع بأن دلالة الألفاظ توقيفية

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila argue that conventional language must be created by humans, since necessary knowledge that God assigned words would entail necessary knowledge of God and undermine moral responsibility.
rows.anchor: خلافا للمعتزلة ، واحتجوا بأن العلم بالصفة إذا كان ضروريا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that God could create necessary knowledge that a human assigner fixed a word's meaning without revealing that the assigner was God.
rows.anchor: يخلق علما ضروريا في القلب بأن واضعا وضع هذا اللفظ لهذا المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the proofs are inconclusive, Razi allows that all languages are divinely instituted, all conventional, or partly each.
rows.anchor: جوزنا أن تكون كل اللغات توقيفية وأن تكون كلها اصطلاحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A simple word cannot explain its own meaning from scratch without circularity, since recognizing its convention requires prior awareness of the word and meaning; learned association resolves the problem.
rows.anchor: لو كان العلم بذلك المعنى مستفادا من ذلك اللفظ لزم الدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The circularity problem does not apply to compounds: convention supplies the simple meanings, and reason combines them to understand the compound.
rows.anchor: أما التركيبات فعقلية ، فلا جرم عند سماع تلك المفردات يعتبر العقل تركيباتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Words signify mental conceptions rather than external objects: changing one's perception of a distant object changes the name used, and contradictory propositions do not make the world both old and originated.
rows.anchor: الألفاظ تدل على المعاني ، لأن المعاني هي التي عناها العاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not every essence can receive a name, because essences are unlimited and an unapprehended item cannot be individually conceived for naming.
rows.anchor: لا يمكن أن تكون جميع الماهيات مسميات بالألفاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Concepts most necessary to communicate, such as commands, prohibitions, generality, and specification, are likeliest to receive words because need supplies strong motivation.
rows.anchor: كل معنى كانت الحاجة إلى التعبير عنه أهم ، كان وضع اللفظ بإزائه أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A familiar word cannot name a hidden concept unknown to the public: motion names observable transition, not a subtle cause; likewise knowledge and power name the evident state, not its hidden ground.
rows.anchor: وجب أن يقال : الحركة اسم لنفس هذا الانتقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿnā denotes the mental conception intended by a speaker; an external thing is called a meaning only derivatively, as what the conception concerns.
rows.anchor: المعنى اسم للصورة الذهنية لا للموجودات الخارجية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some distinctions cannot be defined verbally because language lacks a dedicated term, as with kinds of sweetness; private experiences are also indefinable to listeners who have never conceived them.
rows.anchor: لا سبيل إلى تعريف هذه التفرقة بحسب اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Language serves humans' need to communicate what is in their minds to obtain help; compared with writing, gestures, or clapping, speech is easy to produce, temporary, and combinatorially abundant.
rows.anchor: فاحتاج إلى أن يعرف غيره ما في ضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human perfection is knowledge of truth and action upon good; the body, heart, and respiratory system serve that end, with breathing cooling the heart and expelled air becoming the material of sound.
rows.anchor: كمال الإنسان في أن يعرف الحق لذاته ، والخير لأجل العمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator formed articulatory passages in the throat, tongue, teeth, and lips so breath produces distinct letters and limitless words containing wisdom beyond human grasp.
rows.anchor: وخلق محابس ومقاطع للصوت في الحلق واللسان والأسنان والشفتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spoken kalām is a conventional act by which a living agent reveals inner intentions and beliefs; inner speech, by contrast, is a real attribute like knowledge, power, and will.
rows.anchor: الكلام عبارة عن فعل مخصوص يفعله الحي القادر لأجل أن يعرف غيره ما في ضميره

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila say imperative forms signify the speaker's will, while declarative forms indicate the speaker's belief that the stated matter is so.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : صيغة «افعل » لفظة موضوعة لإرادة الفعل

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi's school distinguishes inward request from will and mental judgment from belief; God's command that an unbeliever believe is not evidence that He wills that belief.
rows.anchor: الطلب النفساني مغاير للإرادة ، والحكم الذهني أمر مغاير للاعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi argues that God commands the unbeliever to believe without willing it: causal determination and God's prior knowledge of disbelief each rule out the contrary belief occurring.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى أمر الكافر بالإيمان ، وهذا متفق عليه ، ولكن لم يرد منه الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A speaker's mental judgment can differ from belief: someone may say the world is eternal while believing it is not, showing the two are distinct.
rows.anchor: وقد يقول القائل بلسانه هذا مع أنه يعتقد أن العالم ليس بقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word's referent may itself be another word: technical terms such as noun, verb, particle, general, and specific name linguistic expressions.
rows.anchor: وقد تكون مدلولاتها أيضا ألفاظا كقولنا : اسم ، وفعل ، وحرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Language is known through transmission, either mass-transmitted or solitary, and through a mix of transmission and reasoning; the majority's combined inference from exception and its effect is weak because it assumes the language-maker accepts the inference.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الطريق تعويل الأكثرين في إثبات أكثر اللغات ، وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some question whether language is mass-transmitted because even Allah, faith, disbelief, and grammatical forms are disputed, Razi says the underlying transmitted usage is certainly mass-transmitted.
rows.anchor: والحق أن ورود هذه الألفاظ في أصول هذه الموارد معلوم بالتواتر
